types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being, typically identified by name and social role. Also called Individual, Celebrity, Artist, Musician, Personality. Examples: Harry Styles, Will Munford, Anne Twist, Gemma Styles.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are all individual people, which aligns with schema.org's Person class definition.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: GenderType
candidates.comment: A GenderType is an Enumeration of genders. Also called sex, gender identity. Examples: Male, Female, NonBinary.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people working together toward a common purpose. Also called Institution, Company, Entity, Corporation, Agency. Examples: Guinness World Records, GWR, Guinness World Record.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: Guinness World Records is a structured organization, matching schema.org's Organization class.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.embedding_query_text: Location: A physical place or venue where events occur. Also called Venue, Site, Place, Stadium, Theater. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Brazil, Mexico, United States.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: The mentions include both stadiums and countries, which are all physical places under schema.org's Place class.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

types.embedding_query_text: EventSeries: A sequence of related events occurring over time. Also called Residency, Tour, ConcertSeries, PerformanceSeries, EventSequence. Examples: 12 sold-out shows, 10 nights in 2025, Together, Together tour, 12-date run.

chosen_type.label: EventSeries
chosen_type.justification: The example 'Together, Together tour' is a recurring event series, fitting schema.org's EventSeries definition.

candidates.label: EventSeries
candidates.comment: An EventSeries is an Event representing a collection of events that share unifying characteristics, such as a recurring festival or a thematic lecture series. Also called event cycle, recurring event, series of events. Examples: The Olympic Games, a monthly book club meeting, a season of a concert series, a weekly farmers market.

candidates.label: VideoGameSeries
candidates.comment: A sequence of related video games, often sharing a common storyline, characters, or gameplay mechanics. Also called game franchise, video game saga, game series. Examples: The Final Fantasy series, The Elder Scrolls series, Grand Theft Auto series.

candidates.label: RadioSeries
candidates.comment: A RadioSeries is a CreativeWorkSeries dedicated to radio broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called radio show, radio program series. Examples: "The Archers", "This American Life", a long-running radio drama, a daily news radio program.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

types.embedding_query_text: MusicalGroup: A collective of musicians performing together as a unit. Also called Band, Group, Ensemble, Collective, MusicalAct. Examples: Coldplay, One Direction.

chosen_type.label: MusicGroup
chosen_type.justification: Coldplay and One Direction are both musical groups, which matches schema.org's MusicGroup class.

candidates.label: MusicGroup
candidates.comment: A MusicGroup, as a PerformingGroup, is an organization of musicians, such as a band or orchestra, or a solo musician. Also called band, musical ensemble, orchestra, solo artist. Examples: The Beatles, New York Philharmonic, Taylor Swift. Distinct from PerformingGroup, which is a broader category for any performance group.

candidates.label: PerformingGroup
candidates.comment: A PerformingGroup is an organization of performers, such as a band, orchestra, or circus. Also called performance ensemble, troupe, artistic group. Examples: Cirque du Soleil, a local theatre company, a dance troupe. Distinct from MusicGroup, which is specifically for musical performers.

candidates.label: DanceGroup
candidates.comment: A DanceGroup is a performing organization specializing in dance, often presenting choreographed performances. Also called dance company, ballet troupe, dance ensemble, dance collective. Examples: Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, Riverdance, New York City Ballet, Bolshoi Ballet.

candidates.label: TheaterGroup
candidates.comment: An organization or company dedicated to producing and performing theatrical works. Also called theater company, drama troupe, acting ensemble. Examples: The Royal Shakespeare Company, Cirque du Soleil, a local amateur dramatics society.

candidates.label: MusicAlbum
candidates.comment: A MusicAlbum, as a MusicPlaylist, is a collection of music tracks released together. Also called album, record album, studio album. Examples: 'Thriller' by Michael Jackson, 'Abbey Road' by The Beatles, a compilation album. Distinct from MusicRecording, which is usually a single song.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time marked by day, month, and year. Also called Timeline, CalendarDate, TemporalMark, Day, Occasion. Examples: 2026-06-12, 2026-07-04, 2010, 2016.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The mentions are specific calendar dates (e.g., '2026-06-12'), aligning with schema.org's Date data type.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

types.embedding_query_text: Audience: A group of people attending or consuming a performance or media. Also called Crowd, Viewers, Listeners, Attendees, Public. Examples: 80,000 people, 80000 attendees, crowd.

chosen_type.label: Audience
chosen_type.justification: The mention '80,000 people' represents a target audience for an event, matching schema.org's Audience class.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

candidates.label: PeopleAudience
candidates.comment: A PeopleAudience, as an Audience, describes a set of characteristics belonging to people, e.g., who compose an item's target audience. Also called demographic group, target audience, human audience. Examples: 'adults aged 18-35', 'students', 'retirees'. Distinct from Audience, which is a broader category including non-human audiences.

candidates.label: MedicalAudience
candidates.comment: An audience type representing target groups for medical web pages. Also called healthcare audience, patient demographic, medical readership. Examples: "patients", "healthcare professionals", "medical researchers", "general public interested in health".

candidates.label: EducationalAudience
candidates.comment: An EducationalAudience is an Audience specifically targeted for educational content or programs. Also called student group, learner demographic, academic audience. Examples: K-12 students, university undergraduates, adult learners, professional development participants.

candidates.label: BusinessAudience
candidates.comment: A BusinessAudience is an Audience defined by characteristics relevant to businesses, such as their industry, size, or role in the value chain. Also called B2B audience, corporate audience, professional audience. Examples: small business owners, IT managers, marketing executives, manufacturing companies. Distinct from PeopleAudience, which targets individual consumers.

types.embedding_query_text: Work: A creative production such as a book, album, or film. Also called Album, Book, Film, Production, CreativeWork. Examples: Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally, fourth studio album.

chosen_type.label: CreativeWork
chosen_type.justification: The example appears to be a music-related creative work, fitting schema.org's CreativeWork class.

mentions: Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally

candidates.label: Movie
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a motion picture film. Also called film, motion picture, cinema. Examples: "The Shawshank Redemption", "Avatar", "Parasite", "Casablanca". Distinct from TVSeries, which is a collection of episodes.

candidates.label: Book
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork consisting of a written or printed work, typically bound together and protected by a cover. Also called publication, volume, printed matter. Examples: "To Kill a Mockingbird", "The Lord of the Rings", "A textbook on physics". Distinct from BookSeries, which is a collection of books.

candidates.label: CreativeWork
candidates.comment: A CreativeWork is the most generic type of intellectual or artistic creation, encompassing a wide range of media and forms. Also called artistic work, intellectual property, creation, content. Examples: A novel, a film, a photograph, a piece of software, a song, a painting.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: MusicPlaylist
candidates.comment: A MusicPlaylist, as a CreativeWork, is an ordered collection of music tracks. Also called playlist, music compilation, track list. Examples: a Spotify playlist, a radio station's daily playlist, a custom mix CD. Distinct from MusicAlbum, which is a formally released collection of tracks.

types.embedding_query_text: Award: A formal recognition given for achievement in a particular field. Also called Recognition, Honor, Prize, Accolade, Distinction. Examples: Brit Awards, Grammy Awards, Ivor Novello Awards.

chosen_type.label: AwardEvent
chosen_type.definition: An event where formal recognition is given for achievements in a particular field.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class directly matches award ceremonies; 'Brit Awards' and 'Grammy Awards' are events, not certifications or roles.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: LiteraryEvent
candidates.comment: An event focused on literature, such as readings, book launches, or discussions. Also called book event, author appearance, literary gathering. Examples: a poetry reading, a book signing, a literary festival, a panel discussion with authors.

chosen_type.label: Event
chosen_type.justification: The X Factor is a TV show, which is a type of event (e.g., broadcast event), but schema.org's Event is the broadest match here.

candidates.label: MusicEvent
candidates.comment: A MusicEvent is an event primarily featuring musical performances. Also called concert, musical performance, gig. Examples: a rock concert, a classical symphony performance, a music festival. Distinct from PerformingArtsEvent, which includes broader performance types like theatre or dance.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: PerformingArtsEvent
candidates.comment: A PerformingArtsEvent is an event featuring live performances of arts like music, theatre, dance, or acrobatics. Also called live performance, show, stage event. Examples: a Broadway play, a ballet performance, a circus show, a stand-up comedy act. Distinct from MusicEvent, which is specifically for music.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: TheaterEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing a live performance in a theater. Also called stage play, theatrical show, drama performance. Examples: a Broadway musical, a local community play, a Shakespearean tragedy.
